_notes: Pinned static builds of the two subprocesses the broadcast pipeline needs.
The session VM fetches these at bootstrap and refuses to use either one on
a sha256 mismatch, exactly as it does with the jamstreamd artifact.
Licensing, and why these are subprocesses: the ffmpeg build below is GPL
(it includes libx264). JamStream links no ffmpeg code, bundles no ffmpeg
code, and speaks to it only over pipes and argv, so the copyleft obligation
stays at the process boundary; the VM downloads the binary from the
publisher named in 'source', which is also where its corresponding source
is published. Keep it that way: linking libav* into jamstreamd would pull
the whole binary under the GPL. MediaMTX is MIT.
Refresh cadence: review at every release and whenever either project ships
a security fix. To refresh an entry, download the URL, run
`shasum -a 256 <file>`, paste the digest here, and run
`cargo test -p jamstream-cloud` (the snapshots pin the rendered output).
Only immutable URLs belong here: a 'latest' or 'release' URL whose content
changes under a fixed path would turn every future boot into a hash
mismatch and refuse to start.
For ffmpeg that means the last autobuild of a month, and nothing else.
BtbN keeps those for years and deletes the daily ones after about a
fortnight, so a mid-month tag stops resolving and every VM that boots
afterwards gets a 404 instead of an encoder. Check the tag ends on the
final day of its month before pinning it.
Verified 2026-08-09 by downloading each artifact and hashing it.
